objects.description: 1-bit run-length encoding decoder class in Pinetime::Tools namespace. It is constructed with a pointer to an encoded buffer and its size, optionally with foreground and background 16-bit colors. Call DecodeNext to write the next chunk of decoded bytes into a provided output buffer up to maxBytes. Internal state members track position in the encoded buffer, bitplane position, current color, and progress. Destruction/ownership: the class does not own the provided buffer (stored as const uint8_t*).
direct_api_constructors: Pinetime::Tools::RleDecoder::RleDecoder(const uint8_t* buffer, size_t size, uint16_t foregroundColor, uint16_t backgroundColor)

functions.name: Pinetime::Tools::RleDecoder::RleDecoder
functions.description: Constructs a 1-bit RLE decoder bound to an encoded input buffer. After construction, call DecodeNext() to incrementally decode into an output buffer up to a caller-specified byte limit per call. The decoder maintains internal state to allow streaming/partial decoding across multiple DecodeNext() calls.
requirements: buffer points to the start of the encoded data and must remain valid and unchanged for the lifetime of the RleDecoder instance (the constructor stores the pointer).
If size > 0, buffer must be non-null; if buffer is null, size must be 0 to avoid dereferencing null.
size specifies the number of bytes available in the encoded buffer; it must not exceed the actual allocated size of the memory referenced by buffer.
The instance must be constructed successfully before any calls to DecodeNext().

functions.name: Pinetime::Tools::RleDecoder::DecodeNext
functions.description: Decodes the next chunk of data from the internal 1-bit RLE stream into the caller-provided output buffer, writing at most maxBytes bytes. Can be called repeatedly to continue decoding where the previous call left off. Intended for incremental/streamed decoding of the provided encoded buffer.
requirements: The RleDecoder instance must have been constructed with a valid encoded buffer prior to this call.
output must be writable memory capable of holding at least maxBytes bytes; if maxBytes > 0, output must be non-null.
maxBytes limits the number of bytes written; behavior for maxBytes == 0 is a no-op decode step (no bytes written).
Callers must not assume thread-safety or reentrancy; use a single thread per instance (stateful decoder).
The function does not return a status; error/EOF signaling behavior is not documented here (unknown).
